{{Short description|Fractal set}}
[[File:Rauzy fractal.png|thumb|300px|Rauzy fractal]]
In mathematics, the '''Rauzy fractal''' is a [[fractal]] set associated with the Tribonacci [[String substitution|substitution]]

: <math>s(1)=12,\  s(2)=13,\  s(3)=1 \,.</math>

It was studied in 1981 by Gérard Rauzy,<ref>{{cite journal | last=Rauzy | first=Gérard | title=Nombres algébriques et substitutions | language=French | zbl=0522.10032 | journal=Bull. Soc. Math. Fr. | volume=110 | pages=147–178 | year=1982 | url=http://archive.numdam.org/ARCHIVE/BSMF/BSMF_1982__110_/BSMF_1982__110__147_0/BSMF_1982__110__147_0.pdf }}</ref>  with the idea of generalizing the dynamic properties of the [[Fibonacci word|Fibonacci morphism]].
That fractal set can be generalized to other maps over a 3-letter alphabet, generating other fractal sets with interesting properties, such as periodic [[tessallation|tiling]] of the plane and [[self-similarity]] in three [[Homothetic transformation|homothetic]] parts.

== Definitions ==

===Tribonacci word===
The '''infinite tribonacci word''' is a [[Word (mathematics)|word]] constructed by iteratively applying the ''Tribonacci'' or ''Rauzy map'' : <math>s(1)=12</math>, <math>s(2)=13</math>, <math>s(3)=1</math>.<ref name=ACOW525>Lothaire (2005) p.525</ref><ref name=PF232>Pytheas Fogg (2002) p.232</ref> It is an example of a [[morphic word]].
Starting from 1, the Tribonacci words are:<ref name=ACOW546>Lothaire (2005) p.546</ref>
* <math>t_0 = 1</math>
* <math>t_1 = 12</math>
* <math>t_2 = 1213</math>
* <math>t_3 = 1213121</math>
* <math>t_4 = 1213121121312</math>
We can show that, for <math>n>2</math>, <math>t_n = t_{n-1}t_{n-2}t_{n-3}</math>; hence the name "[[Tribonacci number|Tribonacci]]".

===Fractal construction===
[[File:Rauzy fractal construction.png|thumb|300px|Construction]]

Consider, now, the space <math>R^3</math> with cartesian coordinates (x,y,z). 
The '''Rauzy fractal''' is constructed this way:<ref name=PF233>Pytheas Fogg (2002) p.233</ref>

1) Interpret the sequence of letters of the infinite Tribonacci word as a sequence of unitary [[Vector (mathematics and physics)|vectors]] of the space, with the following rules (1 = direction x, 2 = direction y, 3 = direction z).

2) Then, build a "stair" by tracing the points reached by this sequence of vectors (see figure). For example, the first points are:
* <math>1 \Rightarrow (1, 0, 0)</math>
* <math>2 \Rightarrow (1, 1, 0)</math>
* <math>1 \Rightarrow (2, 1, 0)</math>
* <math>3 \Rightarrow (2, 1, 1)</math>
* <math>1 \Rightarrow (3, 1, 1)</math>
etc...Every point can be colored according to the corresponding letter, to stress the self-similarity property.

3) Then, project those points on the contracting plane (plane orthogonal to the main direction of propagation of the points, none of those projected points escape to infinity).

== Properties ==
* Can be [[tessellation|tiled]] by three copies of itself, with area reduced by factors <math>k</math>, <math>k^2</math> and <math>k^3</math> with <math>k</math> solution of <math>k^3+k^2+k-1=0</math>: <math>k = \frac{1}{3}\left(-1-\frac{2}{\sqrt[3]{17+3 \sqrt{33}}}+\sqrt[3]{17+3 \sqrt{33}}\right) = 0.543689...</math>.
* Stable under exchanging pieces. We can obtain the same set by exchanging the place of the pieces.
* [[Connected space|Connected]] and simply connected. Has no hole.
* Tiles the plane periodically, by translation.
* The matrix of the Tribonacci map has <math>x^3 - x^2 - x -1</math> as its [[characteristic polynomial]]. Its eigenvalues are a real number  <math>\beta = 1.839286...</math>, called the [[Tribonacci number|Tribonacci constant]], a [[Pisot number]], and two complex conjugates <math>\alpha</math> and <math>\bar \alpha</math> with <math>\alpha \bar \alpha=1/\beta</math>. 
* Its boundary is fractal, and the [[Hausdorff dimension]] of this boundary equals 1.093364... {{oeis|A272408}}, the solution of <math>2|\alpha|^{3s}+|\alpha|^{4s}=1</math>.<ref>{{ cite journal | last=Messaoudi | first=Ali | title=Frontière du fractal de Rauzy et système de numération complexe. (Boundary of the Rauzy fractal and complex numeration system) | language=French | zbl=0968.28005 | journal=Acta Arith. | volume=95 | number=3 | pages=195–224 | year=2000 | url=http://matwbn.icm.edu.pl/ksiazki/aa/aa95/aa9531.pdf }}</ref>

== Variants and generalization ==
For any unimodular substitution of Pisot type, which verifies a coincidence condition (apparently always verified), one can construct a similar set called "Rauzy fractal of the map". They all display [[self-similarity]] and generate, for the examples below, a periodic tiling of the plane.
<gallery>
Image:Rauzy1.png|s(1)=12, s(2)=31, s(3)=1
Image:Rauzy2.png|s(1)=12, s(2)=23, s(3)=312
Image:Rauzy3.png|s(1)=123, s(2)=1, s(3)=31
Image:Rauzy4.png|s(1)=123, s(2)=1, s(3)=1132
</gallery>
